summary: This breaks the grep's wording, not what plan §4.9 is for. The two kit files from PR #53 contain the spike's results-folder path, `spikes/netcode-proof/results/`. They use it as data: the folder must exist and hold committed results, `list` writes its list there and `pack` reads it. They import, run and read no spike code. My ruling (REFS-KIT) is a tightened form of option (a). The refs step lets exactly these two full paths name that one folder and nothing else of the spike. Any other `spikes/` text in them still fails, and so does any other file outside `spikes/` that names it. The change is one new test with three planted bugs, plus one line each in plan §4.2 and §4.9. No kit file changes, and no mark, run or cost changes, so it does not need Mustafa's word first; he is told in the next report and can still say no (one commit to undo). Order: the fix as its own commit first, then the merge commit on its own, then real packs, then C62H-BOUND's build from the merged head. I checked all of this in memory against git objects: no worktree was made and no repository file was written except my notes. Before the fix the merged tree fails with exactly the two kit files; after it, the tree passes; the new test passes and each of the three planted bugs fails it.
clash:
The check broke on its wording, not on its purpose. Plan §4.9's purpose comes from ADR 0002:145-146: "Nothing in `crates/` or `packages/` imports from `legacy/` ... or from `spikes/` (the same rule; spikes are throwaway)". In other words, the foundation never depends on the spike, and the spike can be deleted cleanly. Both still hold.

`.claude/scripts/kept-logs.mjs` (main 53272a1, sha256 c9109ab4…) names `spikes/` twice:
- :8, a header comment;
- :37, `const RESULTS = 'spikes/netcode-proof/results/'`.

What it does with that path:
- It is a guard. checkSet (:118-133) refuses a `--results` folder that is not under that path or does not hold the set's 12 hex digits. It also refuses a folder that does not exist, that has no results committed in the ref, or that has uncommitted changes.
- It is where the list lives. `list` writes raw-logs.sha256 there (:144). `pack` checks that the list is committed and pushed (:209-215), then reads it.
- It imports no spike module, runs no spike program and reads no spike source. Its only tie is the committed results folder of a closed run set: the data his rule protects.

`.claude/scripts/kept-logs.test.mjs` (sha256 20de2081…) names it at :24, :207-210 and :300 (:214 is 'spikes' without a slash). Every one of these is inside scratch repositories the test builds in the system temp folder. It never reads the real `spikes/` folder; the dry run reads a real run-set folder under `.gate/`.

Neither file is in `crates/` or `packages/`, and nothing there uses them (grep). Taking `spikes/netcode-proof/results/` out of either file leaves no `spikes/` text in it (checked).

If the spike is deleted, nothing breaks. `list` and `pack` refuse (exit 2, nothing removed), and `cache` and the kit tests are unaffected. So only the grep's wording is hit: "any tracked file outside the skips that contains `spikes/`" (check.mjs:1840-1853).

The plan already allows this kind of exception. §4.2 (plan.md:451-453) gives W-PR's workflow file "an exception that names it by path, in the same change".

Why no review saw it: PR #53 targeted main, where neither the spike nor check.mjs exists.

fix.choice:
A tightened form of option (a): the refs step lets exactly the two full paths, `.claude/scripts/kept-logs.mjs` and `.claude/scripts/kept-logs.test.mjs`, name `spikes/netcode-proof/results/`. Before the grep, that folder name is taken out of those two files and nothing else is. Any other `spikes/` text in them still fails: the spike's code, its crates, its root, or the folder name without the trailing slash. Every other `.claude/`, `tools/` or root file that names `spikes/` still fails. A comment names his KEPT-LOGS rule and says why. The refs step's PASS line names §4.9's one exception, so the line stays true once the kit files are in the tree. The plan gets the matching lines in §4.2 and §4.9.

Options weighed and not chosen:
- (a) as given (skip the whole file): looser for no gain. It would let either kit file later import spike code unseen; planted bug P2 shows the new test catches that.
- (b) skip all of `.claude/scripts/`, or all of `.claude/`: far too broad. A future hook or script that runs spike code is exactly the dependency §4.9 is there to catch; planted bug P1 shows the test catches it, including a stray `kept-logs.mjs.orig`.
- (c1) edit the kit files so they don't spell `spikes/` (for example build the string in pieces, or take the results root as an argument): that changes text he froze (KIT-FREEZE-2, his yes needed), and building the string in pieces would just hide the path from the grep.
- (c2) pin the two files by sha256 instead of by path: it duplicates the freeze that his yes and the PR review already hold. It is also brittle, because the step reads working-tree bytes (line endings) and needs a check.mjs edit whenever the kit changes.
- (c3) wait to take main in until the spike is on main: against his KL-MERGE words, and it blocks every pack.

Known limit, stated in the comment: a `..` after the results-folder name is not read. kept-logs.test.mjs:208 names one on purpose, as a path the script must refuse, so forbidding `..` there would fail the real file. Review of a kit change, which needs his yes anyway, is the wall.

check_mjs.new:
if (KEPT_LOGS_FILES.includes(f)) text = text.replaceAll(KEPT_LOGS_RESULTS, "");
    if (text.includes("spikes/")) problems.push(`${f} references spikes/`);

check_mjs.old: return { ok: problems.length === 0, out: problems.join("\n") || `${files.length} tracked files: none outside spikes/ references it` };
check_mjs.new: return { ok: problems.length === 0, out: problems.join("\n") || `${files.length} tracked files: none outside spikes/ references it (§4.9's one exception: the KEPT-LOGS kit files may name its results folder)` };

fix.planted_bug:
Main planted bug P1, option (b)'s broad skip: in the new check.mjs line, `if (KEPT_LOGS_FILES.includes(f)) text` becomes `if (f.startsWith(".claude/scripts/")) text`. The new test fails by name: `.claude/scripts/checkpoint.mjs` and `.claude/scripts/kept-logs.mjs.orig` are no longer flagged.

Two more plants, to prove the narrowing and the exception itself:
- P2, a whole-file skip: the new line becomes `if (KEPT_LOGS_FILES.includes(f)) continue;`. The new test fails in its loop: kit files naming `spikes/netcode-proof/check.mjs` are not flagged (actual [], expected both).
- P3, no exception: the new line is deleted. The new test fails: both kit files are flagged.

Under all three plants, the old test ('only code outside spikes/ is read for references to it') still passes. Plant each one in a scratch copy under .gate/, as with earlier plants; never in the main folder.

order:
1. REFS-KIT first, as its own commit on this branch, before the merge. It does not go inside the merge commit: a merge that also changes logic hides the change from the merge's diff and leaves no commit where the fix alone can be checked.
   - This ruling is its plan and its approval. Apply the six edits word for word with the Edit tool. None is a kit or gate file, so there is no ask.
   - Evidence: `check.mjs --only refs,self` PASS, with self +1 test and 0 failed. The three plants, in a scratch copy under .gate/, each fail the new test by name while the old test passes.
   - Then check.mjs whole and the gate (`--no-smoke`, as on the card); commit and push. The advisor checks the pushed head (that check is not a review round).
2. Then the merge commit on its own: `git merge --no-ff --no-commit origin/main`, merge_main_53.py for docs/STATUS.md, and nothing else.
   - check.mjs whole: refs must PASS with the line naming §4.9's exception. Then the gate; push. The advisor checks that head.
3. Only then the first real kept-logs `list`/`pack`, per §11:
   - never while a build or a run set is running;
   - the P0 raw-log folder that C62H-BOUND-YES's re-judge reads stays unpacked until that judge call has run.
   - Report the free space before and after, as his KL-MERGE words ask.
4. C62H-BOUND's build:
   - Its brief may be written and checked now; that is not an edit.
   - Its first edit starts from step 2's merged head, in its worktree, not on bedca79. Four reasons: his KL-MERGE words put taking main in next; the build runs check.mjs after each step and should do so on the tree that ships, kit files included; its design's step 5 may need a pack before the judged runs, and a pack needs main in and may not overlap a build; and one change-set at a time.
   - The files do not overlap (C62H-BOUND's design: "No change to ... check.mjs"; REFS-KIT touches only check.mjs, check.test.mjs and plan.md). So if step 1 or 2 stalls, for example because he objects, the build may start from the branch head at that point, with main taken in after it. No pack runs before main is in.
follow_up:
When the spike is deleted (plan §4.9's last bullet; the advisor confirms the deleting change-set):
- kept-logs.mjs's `list` and `pack` then refuse every set, because the `--results` folder no longer exists (exit 2, nothing removed). `cache` is unaffected. The kit tests still pass, since they build their own scratch repositories. The REFS-KIT exception goes away with check.mjs.
- Before that change-set merges, every raw-log folder of a closed set is either packed or recorded as kept. The archives stay under `.gate/netcode-proof-test/kept-logs/`, and their lists stay in git at the closing SHA that ADR 0001's results name, so each archive can still be checked.
- The change-set proposes to Mustafa what becomes of §11's raw-log part, the two scripts' `list` and `pack`, and their two REPO_MAP rows: retire them, or keep them for a named successor spike. That is a kit change (risk tier 2, his yes, security-auditor's review).

Process line for STATUS: when a change bound for main names a path under `spikes/`, run the spike branch's refs step on it before its review closes. PR #53's review could not see this clash, because main has no spike.
